title: CREST challenge

category.description: C1 Constrained, C2 Counterfactual, C3 Cross-Domain, C4 Meta-Creativity, C5 Open-Ended

domain.$comment: Union of two datasets' vocabularies: the six original science domains (crest_challenges.jsonl) and the six AI/ML domains (crest_aiml_challenges.jsonl). One schema rather than two because everything else about the item format is identical; the enum still catches typos, since a misspelling is in neither set. It no longer catches a science item using an AI/ML domain or vice versa -- the datasets are separate files, so that is not a confusion the loader can make.

query.description: the challenge prompt; must require multi-source web synthesis

known_answers.description: dated list of already-known answers; baseline for New

expert_baseline.description: JUDGE-HIDDEN since 2026-07-30. Was the Surprising anchor; an ablation showed withholding it moved Surprising by -0.02, so it anchored nothing, and in 7 items it carried the author's enumeration of the intended surprises. Retained for provenance and possible future use (e.g. a human-scored arm), but NOT sent to judge/score.py::_judge_prompt.

author_expected_surprises.description: JUDGE-HIDDEN. Author-written enumeration of the surprises the baseline is not supposed to anticipate, plus any rubric directives that were embedded in expert_baseline. Split out because piping it to the judge made Surprising into graded recall against an author-written key: an answer containing the listed content scored high by construction, and a different genuine surprise earned nothing. NOT read by judge/score.py::_judge_prompt -- keep it that way.

description: Validated on load by harness.run_crest.load_challenges. Previously this file was never applied: no jsonschema import existed anywhere in the repo, so `required` was decorative and category_name (present in all 50 items) validated silently because additionalProperties was unset. v2.0.0 removed `predicted_direction` (moved to analysis/preregistration.yaml; it was a 5-row lookup on `category` and, living in editable data, could not evidence ordering) and `category_name` (derivable from `category`; one item shipped a long-form value so groupby yielded 6 categories). v3.0.0 moved `rationale` to questions/item_design.jsonl (read by no code at runtime; 20% of bytes) -- ci_check.sh enforces the id bijection.
